I've been farming this land since I was a young man. My father farmed it too. In Quzhou, you grow wheat in winter and corn in summer — that's what the land is for, that's what the market wants, and that's what I know. I'm not going to change that at 70.

I have 12 mu of contracted land. My two sons are in the city. It's just me and my wife now. My knees are bad, so I hire machines to plow and harvest — I can't manage that by hand anymore. But I still do the spraying and fertilizing myself, and I keep a small vegetable plot that my wife tends mostly.

For the wheat this October, I'll use the improved variety seeds from the village cooperative — the same kind I used last two years, yield was fine. I'll put down compound base fertilizer at planting, mix it into the soil. Then in March I'll top-dress with urea when the plants start jointing. Three irrigations: one before the cold really sets in, one in spring when the shoots are coming up, one around heading if it looks dry. Two pesticide sprays — powdery mildew comes every year, and the aphids show up near heading time.

Right after wheat harvest in June I'll plant hybrid maize on the same 10 mu, no-till, straight into the stubble. Zhengdan 958 type seed — reliable, everybody around here uses it. I apply more nitrogen for corn than wheat, it needs it. Usually enough rain in July and August so I only irrigate once, maybe not at all if the rains come. One spray for corn borer.

I keep 2 mu for vegetables — cabbage, garlic, some hot peppers. What we don't eat I sell at the village market. That's a little extra income and it keeps us fed well.
